question.text: When does a put option buyer choose to exercise the option?

answer.text: When the underlying price is below the strike price
When the underlying price is above the strike price
When the underlying price equals the strike price
When the premium increases above the strike price

explanation.text: The Logic: A put gives the right to sell at the strike price. The workbook states that the put buyer exercises when the GOI security (underlying) price is below the strike price, since the buyer can then sell at a higher-than-market strike. The Trap: The underlying being above the strike is the call-buyer's exercise condition. At-the-money exercise gives zero cash flow. Note: Think of a put as insurance -- you "claim" only when the price falls below the protected level (strike).
